This is the R twin of the Python guide
[`distributions-for-actuaries-counts-aggregates.md`](distributions-for-actuaries-counts-aggregates.md).
It recomputes the worked examples and problem answers of chapters 3 and 4 and
the aggregate limits of section 6.4 of CAS Monograph 2, *Distributions for
Actuaries* by David Bahnemann (2015). The sections and numbers are the same,
because the R package runs the same Rust code. Read the Python guide for the
discussion of each result. The companion R guide,
[`distributions-for-actuaries-claim-size.qmd`](distributions-for-actuaries-claim-size.qmd),
covers chapters 2, 5 and 6. `R/prospicio/tests/test-guides.R` requires each
chunk to print exactly the text under it.

## 1. Translating the parameters

| Monograph | prospicio (R) |
|---|---|
| Poisson λ | `poisson_count(λ)` |
| binomial (m, p) | `binomial_count(m, p)` |
| negative binomial (α, ν), Var = ν + ν²/α | `negative_binomial_count(α, ν/α)` |
| mean ν and contagion γ | `claim_count(ν, 1 + γν)` |
| Poisson mixed by a gamma with mean ν and shape α | `mixed_poisson_count(ν, 1/√α, "gamma")` |
| method of moments | `negative_binomial_count_from_mean_variance(m, v)` |
| any count on 0, 1, 2, ... | `empirical_count(probs)` |

`compare()` builds the book-against-prospicio tables below.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(prospicio)
library(gt)

num <- function(x, digits = 0) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
row <- function(label, book, ours, digits = 4) list(label = label, book = book, ours = ours, digits = digits)
compare <- function(rows, title, subtitle = NULL) {
  frame <- data.frame(row = vapply(rows, function(r) r$label, ""),
                      book = vapply(rows, function(r) r$book, 0),
                      prospicio = vapply(rows, function(r) r$ours, 0))
  digits <- vapply(rows, function(r) r$digits, 0)
  table <- gt(frame, rowname_col = "row") |> tab_header(title, subtitle)
  for (d in unique(digits)) {
    table <- fmt_number(table, columns = c(book, prospicio), rows = which(digits == d), decimals = d)
  }
  table
}
chi_square <- function(observed, probs) {
  e <- sum(observed) * probs
  sum((observed - e)^2 / e)
}
```

## 2. The Poisson and the binomial

```{r}
#| label: poisson
rows <- list(row("Ex 3.1, 30 days, Pr{N = 0}", 0.9138, pmf(binomial_count(30, 0.003), 0)),
             row("Ex 3.1, 30 days, Pr{N = 1}", 0.0825, pmf(binomial_count(30, 0.003), 1)),
             row("Ex 3.1, 365 days, Pr{N = 2}", 0.2009, pmf(binomial_count(365, 0.003), 2)))
for (case in list(list(1.0, c(0.9608, 0.0384, 0.0008)), list(1.5, c(0.9418, 0.0565, 0.0017)))) {
  for (n in 0:2) {
    rows <- c(rows, list(row(sprintf("Ex 3.2, %.1f years, Pr{N = %d}", case[[1]], n), case[[2]][n + 1],
                             pmf(poisson_count(0.04 * case[[1]]), n))))
  }
}
for (case in list(c(6, 0.0012), c(15, 0.0069), c(24, 0.0164))) {
  rows <- c(rows, list(row(sprintf("P3.4, %d months, Pr{N = 2}", case[1]), case[2],
                           pmf(poisson_count(0.10 * case[1] / 12), 2))))
}
compare(rows, "Ex 3.1, Ex 3.2 and P3.4: binomial and Poisson probabilities")
```

```{r}
#| label: poisson-fit
policies <- c(868, 118, 11, 2, 1)
lam <- sum((0:4) * policies) / sum(policies)
p <- poisson_count(lam)
rows <- list(row("Ex 3.3, rate", 0.15, lam, 2))
for (k in 0:3) {
  rows <- c(rows, list(row(sprintf("Ex 3.3, Pr{N = %d}", k), c(0.8607, 0.1291, 0.0097, 0.0005)[k + 1], pmf(p, k))))
}
rows <- c(rows, list(
  row("Ex 3.3, chi-square", 2.43, chi_square(c(868, 118, 14), c(pmf(p, 0), pmf(p, 1), 1 - cdf(p, 1))), 2),
  row("Ex 3.8, Pr{N >= 5}, 100 x 0.035", 0.2746, 1 - cdf(poisson_count(3.5), 4))))
for (case in list(c(2.5, 0.7576), c(6.25, 0.1303), c(2.0, 0.8571), c(4.0, 0.4335))) {
  rows <- c(rows, list(row(sprintf("P3.3, Pr{N <= 3}, rate %s", format(case[1], nsmall = 1)), case[2],
                           cdf(poisson_count(case[1]), 3))))
}
rows <- c(rows, list(
  row("P3.30, Pr{N >= 6}, 20 cars x 0.30", 0.5543, 1 - cdf(poisson_count(6), 5)),
  row("P3.31, policies with a claim, of 8,000", 624, 8000 * (1 - pmf(poisson_count(650 / 8000), 0)), 0)))
compare(rows, "Ex 3.3, Ex 3.8, P3.3, P3.30 and P3.31: fitting and using a Poisson")
```

## 3. Parameter uncertainty: mixed Poissons

```{r}
#| label: mixed
rates <- c(0.10, 0.35, 0.70, 1.40); weights <- c(0.20, 0.40, 0.30, 0.10)
mixed <- sapply(0:5, function(n) sum(weights * sapply(rates, function(r) pmf(poisson_count(r), n))))
m <- sum(weights * rates)
v <- m + sum(weights * rates^2) - m^2
geo <- mixed_poisson_count(0.25, 1, "gamma")
pmf_table <- data.frame(
  n = sprintf("N = %d", 0:5),
  mixed_book = c(0.6365, 0.2556, 0.0788, 0.0218, 0.0056, 0.0013), mixed = mixed,
  poisson_book = c(0.6005, 0.3063, 0.0781, 0.0133, 0.0017, 0.0002), poisson = pmf(poisson_count(m), 0:5),
  geo_book = c(0.8, 0.16, 0.032, 0.0064, 0.0013, 0.0003), geo_mixed = pmf(geo, 0:5),
  geo = pmf(geometric_count(0.25), 0:5)
)
gt(pmf_table, rowname_col = "n") |>
  tab_header("Ex 3.4 and Ex 3.5: probability of N claims") |>
  tab_spanner("Ex 3.4, mixed Poisson", columns = c(mixed_book, mixed)) |>
  tab_spanner("Ex 3.4, Poisson with mean 0.51", columns = c(poisson_book, poisson)) |>
  tab_spanner("Ex 3.5, exponential mixing", columns = c(geo_book, geo_mixed, geo)) |>
  fmt_number(columns = -n, decimals = 4) |>
  cols_label(mixed_book = "book", mixed = "prospicio", poisson_book = "book", poisson = "prospicio",
             geo_book = "book", geo_mixed = "prospicio", geo = "geometric")
```

```{r}
#| label: mixed-figure
library(ggplot2, exclude = "layer")   # keeps prospicio's layer()

           data = data.frame(n = 0:5, p = pmf(poisson_count(m), 0:5))) +

       title = "Ex 3.4: the mixture against the Poisson with the same mean") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

```{r}
#| label: gamma-mixtures
nb <- negative_binomial_count(2, 1)
rows <- list(row("Ex 3.4, Var[N]", 0.6439, v),
             row("Ex 3.5, Var[N]", 0.3125, variance(geo)),
             row("P3.11, mean", 2, mean(nb), 0),
             row("P3.11, variance", 4, variance(nb), 0),
             row("P3.11, Pr{N <= 3}", 0.8125, cdf(nb, 3)))
nb <- negative_binomial_count_from_mean_variance(0.100, 0.100 + 0.005)
for (n in 0:3) {
  rows <- c(rows, list(row(sprintf("P3.12, Pr{N = %d}", n), c(0.9070, 0.0864, 0.0062, 0.0004)[n + 1], pmf(nb, n))))
}
rows <- c(rows, list(
  row("P3.13, Var, Poisson 0.75", 0.7500, variance(poisson_count(0.75))),
  row("P3.13, Var, two-point mixture", 0.8175, 0.75 + (0.75 * 0.6^2 + 0.25 * 1.2^2 - 0.75^2)),
  row("P3.13, Var, exponential mixture", 1.3125, variance(mixed_poisson_count(0.75, 1)))))
compare(rows, "Ex 3.4, Ex 3.5 and P3.11 to P3.13: variances and gamma mixtures")
```

## 4. The negative binomial and contagion

```{r}
#| label: negbin
nb_moments <- function(counts) {
  k <- seq_along(counts) - 1
  m1 <- sum(k * counts) / sum(counts)
  c(m1, sum(k^2 * counts) / sum(counts) - m1^2)
}
rows <- list()
for (case in list(list("Ex 3.6", c(4429, 528, 39, 3, 1), c(0.1238, 2.44285, 0.7753)),
                  list("P3.15", c(8956, 907, 120, 15, 2), c(0.1200, 0.685714, 0.3288)))) {
  mv <- nb_moments(case[[2]])
  nb <- negative_binomial_count_from_mean_variance(mv[1], mv[2])
  probs <- c(pmf(nb, 0:2), 1 - cdf(nb, 2))
  observed <- c(case[[2]][1:3], sum(case[[2]][-(1:3)]))
  rows <- c(rows, list(row(paste0(case[[1]], ", mean"), case[[3]][1], mv[1]),
                       row(paste0(case[[1]], ", alpha = r"), case[[3]][2], nb@r, 5),
                       row(paste0(case[[1]], ", chi-square"), case[[3]][3], chi_square(observed, probs))))
  if (case[[1]] == "Ex 3.6") {
    for (k in 0:3) {
      rows <- c(rows, list(row(sprintf("Ex 3.6, Pr{N = %d}", k), c(0.8862, 0.1044, 0.0087, 0.0006)[k + 1],
                               pmf(nb, k))))
    }
  }
}
compare(rows, "Ex 3.6 and P3.15: negative binomials fitted by moments")
```

```{r}
#| label: contagion
nb <- claim_count(1, 1 + 0.2 * 1)
contagion <- function(counts) {
  m <- sum(sapply(counts, mean)); v <- sum(sapply(counts, variance))
  (v - m) / m^2
}
book <- c(0.4019, 0.3349, 0.1674, 0.0651, 0.0217, 0.0065)
rows <- lapply(0:5, function(n) row(sprintf("P3.28, Pr{N = %d}", n), book[n + 1], pmf(nb, n)))
rows <- c(rows, list(
  row("Ex 3.9, contagion, 20 policies, nu 0.15, gamma 0.4", 0.020,
      contagion(rep(list(claim_count(0.15, 1 + 0.4 * 0.15)), 20)), 3),
  row("P3.29, contagion, three lines", 0.1000,
      contagion(list(claim_count(10, 1 + 0.35 * 10), claim_count(25, 1 + 0.20 * 25), poisson_count(5))))))
compare(rows, "P3.28, Ex 3.9 and P3.29: contagion")
```

## 5. Aggregate claims and their moments

`compound_distribution()` uses Panjer's recursion by default. Pass
`method = "fft"` for the FFT, as the Python guide does. R indexes from 1, so the
probability of a total of `k` steps is `probs[k + 1]`.

```{r}
#| label: aggregate
agg <- compound_distribution(empirical_count(c(0.6, 0.3, 0.1)),
                             grid_distribution(100, c(0, 0.4, 0.5, 0.1)), 16, method = "fft")
book <- c(0.6, 0.72, 0.886, 0.956, 0.989, 0.999, 1.0)
rows <- lapply(0:6, function(k) row(sprintf("Ex 4.1, F_S(%d)", 100 * k), book[k + 1], cdf(agg, 100 * k)))
rows <- c(rows, list(row("Ex 4.1, E[S]", 85, mean(agg), 0), row("Ex 4.1, Var[S]", 15055, variance(agg), 0)))
compare(rows, "Ex 4.1: a small discrete aggregate")
```

```text
Ex 4.1, F_S(200)  0.8860     0.8860
Ex 4.1, F_S(300)  0.9560     0.9560
```

```{r}
#| label: aggregate-ex42
m <- compound_moments(poisson_count(2.5), gamma_distribution(3, 400))
poisson_gamma_cdf <- function(s, lam, shape, scale, terms = 400) {
  n <- poisson_count(lam)
  if (s <= 0) return(pmf(n, 0))
  k <- 1:(terms - 1)
  pmf(n, 0) + sum(pmf(n, k) * sapply(k, function(j) cdf(gamma_distribution(shape * j, scale), s)))
}
S <- c(0, 500, 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 6000, 8000, 10000)
book <- c(0.0821, 0.1096, 0.1867, 0.3755, 0.5613, 0.7152, 0.9013, 0.9723, 0.9934)
rows <- list(row("Ex 4.2, E[S]", 3000, m[["mean"]], 0),
             row("Ex 4.2, Var[S]", 4800000, m[["variance"]], 0),
             row("Ex 4.2, skewness", 0.9129, m[["skew"]]))
rows <- c(rows, lapply(seq_along(S), function(i) {
  row(sprintf("Ex 4.2, F(%s)", num(S[i])), book[i], poisson_gamma_cdf(S[i], 2.5, 3, 400))
}))
compare(rows, "Ex 4.2 and Table 4.1: Poisson 2.5 with gamma (3; 400) claims")
```

## 6. Approximations by matching moments

```{r}
#| label: approximations
cases <- list(
  list("Table 4.3", 4, 2.5, 3, 400, c(0, 2000, 4000, 6000, 8000),
       c(0.0821, 0.3755, 0.7152, 0.9013, 0.9723), c(0.0855, 0.3240, 0.6760, 0.9145, 0.9888),
       c(0.0459, 0.3680, 0.7185, 0.9038, 0.9724)),
  list("Table 4.4", 5, 10, 0.05, 6000, c(0, 2000, 6000, 10000, 18000),
       c(0.00005, 0.5922, 0.8401, 0.9294, 0.9846), c(0.2451, 0.4090, 0.7549, 0.9463, 0.9997),
       c(0.1228, 0.5886, 0.8402, 0.9298, 0.9847)),
  list("P4.13", 4, 8, 0.2, 3750, c(0, 3000, 9000, 15000, 27000),
       c(0.0003, 0.3420, 0.7774, 0.9349, 0.9954), c(0.1241, 0.2819, 0.7181, 0.9584, 1.0000),
       c(0.0263, 0.3362, 0.7782, 0.9356, 0.9953))
)
moment_frame <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cases, function(cs) {
  m <- compound_moments(poisson_count(cs[[3]]), gamma_distribution(cs[[4]], cs[[5]]))
  data.frame(case = cs[[1]], mean = m[["mean"]], sd = sqrt(m[["variance"]]), skewness = m[["skew"]])
}))
gt(moment_frame, rowname_col = "case") |>
  tab_header("Tables 4.3, 4.4 and P4.13: the aggregate's moments") |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(mean, sd), decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_number(columns = skewness, decimals = 4)
```

```text
Table 4.3  3,000  2,191    0.9129
Table 4.4  3,000  4,347    2.8293
P4.13      6,000  5,196    1.5877
```

```{r}
#| label: approximations-table
approx_frame <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cases, function(cs) {
  freq <- poisson_count(cs[[3]]); sev <- gamma_distribution(cs[[4]], cs[[5]]); S <- cs[[6]]
  approx <- function(kind) sapply(S, function(s) approximation_cdf(moment_approximation(freq, sev, kind), s))
  data.frame(case = sprintf("%s, s = %s", cs[[1]], num(S)),
             exact_book = cs[[7]],
             exact = sapply(S, poisson_gamma_cdf, lam = cs[[3]], shape = cs[[4]], scale = cs[[5]]),
             normal_book = cs[[8]], normal = approx("normal"),
             sgamma_book = cs[[9]], sgamma = approx("shifted_gamma"),
             slognormal = approx("shifted_lognormal"))
}))
gt(approx_frame, rowname_col = "case") |>
  tab_header("F(s) by the exact series and three approximations") |>
  tab_spanner("exact series", columns = c(exact_book, exact)) |>
  tab_spanner("normal approximation", columns = c(normal_book, normal)) |>
  tab_spanner("shifted gamma", columns = c(sgamma_book, sgamma)) |>
  fmt_number(columns = -case, decimals = 4) |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(exact_book, exact), rows = 6, decimals = 5) |>   # Table 4.4 at s = 0
  cols_label(exact_book = "book", exact = "prospicio", normal_book = "book", normal = "prospicio",
             sgamma_book = "book", sgamma = "prospicio", slognormal = "shifted lognormal")
```

The curves show Tables 4.3 and 4.4:

```{r}
#| label: approximations-figure
curves <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cases[1:2], function(cs) {
  freq <- poisson_count(cs[[3]]); sev <- gamma_distribution(cs[[4]], cs[[5]])
  mo <- compound_moments(freq, sev)
  xs <- (mo[["mean"]] + 4.5 * sqrt(mo[["variance"]])) * (0:40) / 40
  approx <- function(kind) sapply(xs, function(s) approximation_cdf(moment_approximation(freq, sev, kind), s))
  data.frame(case = sprintf("%s: skewness %.1f", cs[[1]], mo[["skew"]]),
             s = rep(xs, 3), cdf = c(sapply(xs, poisson_gamma_cdf, lam = cs[[3]], shape = cs[[4]],
                                            scale = cs[[5]], terms = 60),
                                     approx("normal"), approx("shifted_gamma")),
             curve = rep(c("exact", "normal", "shifted gamma"), each = length(xs)))
}))
curves$curve <- factor(curves$curve, levels = c("exact", "normal", "shifted gamma"))
ggplot(curves, aes(s, cdf, colour = curve, linewidth = curve)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~case, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(exact = "grey75", normal = "#F8766D", "shifted gamma" = "#00BFC4")) +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(exact = 2.5, normal = 0.7, "shifted gamma" = 0.7)) +
  labs(x = "total claims s", y = "F(s)", colour = NULL, linewidth = NULL,
       title = "Tables 4.3 and 4.4: the exact distribution and two approximations") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## 7. Recursion and Fourier inversion

```{r}
#| label: recursion
agg <- compound_distribution(poisson_count(1.75), grid_distribution(1000, c(0, 0.20, 0.40, 0.20, 0.15, 0.05)), 64)
book <- c(0.1738, 0.0608, 0.1323, 0.1046, 0.117, 0.0932, 0.0786, 0.0641)
rows <- lapply(0:7, function(k) row(sprintf("Ex 4.4, f_S(%s)", num(1000 * k)), book[k + 1], agg@probs[k + 1]))
rows <- c(rows, lapply(list(c(9000, 0.9121), c(12000, 0.9729), c(16000, 0.9955)), function(x) {
  row(sprintf("Ex 4.4, F_S(%s)", num(x[1])), x[2], cdf(agg, x[1]))
}))
compare(rows, "Ex 4.4: Panjer's recursion, a Poisson 1.75")
```

```{r}
#| label: midpoint
S <- c(500, 1000, 2000, 4000, 6000, 10000)
ex_45 <- list()
for (case in list(list(100, c(0.1158, 0.1956, 0.3852, 0.7218, 0.9042, 0.9937)),
                  list(20, c(0.1108, 0.1885, 0.3775, 0.7165, 0.9019, 0.9935)))) {
  h <- case[[1]]
  grid <- discretize(gamma_distribution(3, 400), h, 6000 / h + 1, "rounding")
  agg <- compound_distribution(poisson_count(2.5), grid, 30000 / h)
  ex_45[[as.character(h)]] <- list(book = case[[2]], ours = cdf(agg, S))
  cat(sprintf("Ex 4.5  step %3.0f  grid mean %s  variance %s\n", h, num(mean(grid), 2), num(variance(grid))))
}
```

## 8. Simulation

```{r}
#| label: simulation
years <- total(total(simulate_events(poisson_count(2.5), gamma_distribution(3, 400), 10000, 2015)))
sim <- cdf(years, 3000)
exact <- poisson_gamma_cdf(3000, 2.5, 3, 400)
cat(sprintf("Ex 4.14  F(3,000): book's sample 0.5599, exact %.4f, within two standard errors here: %s\n",
            exact, abs(sim - exact) < 2 * sqrt(exact * (1 - exact) / 10000)))
cat(sprintf("Ex 4.13  lognormal (4.956; 2.3), 1.5 claims a year: E[S] = %s (book 3,000)\n",
            num(1.5 * mean(lognormal(4.956, 2.3)))))
```

## 9. Aggregate limits

Ex 6.6's lognormal has μ = 7.6, not the printed 7.000 (see the Python guide).
The stop-loss of the shifted gamma is a gamma's. It uses the `parameters` (shape,
scale and shift) of `moment_approximation()`.

```{r}
#| label: aggregate-limits
size <- lognormal(7.6, 2.4)
count <- claim_count(1.2, 1 + 0.1 * 1.2)
basic <- mean(count) * lev(size, 500e3)
h <- 250
capped_2m <- discretize(size, h, 2e6 / h + 1, "local_moment")
m <- compound_moments(count, capped_2m)
compare(list(row("Ex 6.6, E[S], 500K per claim", 26092, basic, 0),
             row("Ex 6.6, E[S], 2M per claim", 34006, mean(count) * lev(size, 2e6), 0),
             row("Ex 6.6, sd of S, 2M per claim", 151311, sqrt(m[["variance"]]), 0),
             row("Ex 6.6, skewness, 2M per claim", 9.4728, m[["skew"]])),
        "Ex 6.6: lognormal (7.6; 2.4) claims, 1.2 expected claims, contagion 0.1")
```

```text
                                   book  prospicio
Ex 6.6, E[S], 500K per claim     26,092     26,091
Ex 6.6, E[S], 2M per claim       34,006     34,006
Ex 6.6, sd of S, 2M per claim   151,311    151,312
Ex 6.6, skewness, 2M per claim   9.4728     9.4728
```

```{r}
#| label: removed
shifted_gamma_excess <- function(severity, L) {
  a <- moment_approximation(count, severity, "shifted_gamma")$parameters
  stop_loss(gamma_distribution(a[["shape"]], a[["scale"]]), L - a[["shift"]])
}
sg <- shifted_gamma_excess(capped_2m, 3e6)
agg <- compound_distribution(count, capped_2m, 2^16, method = "fft")
exact <- stop_loss(agg, 3e6)
removed <- data.frame(row = c("removed by a 3M aggregate limit", "I(2M, 3M)"),
                      book = c(91, 1.2998),
                      shifted = c(sg, (m[["mean"]] - sg) / basic),
                      exact = c(exact, (m[["mean"]] - exact) / basic))
gt(removed, rowname_col = "row") |>
  tab_header("Ex 6.6: a 3M aggregate limit on 2M claims") |>
  fmt_number(columns = -row, rows = 1, decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_number(columns = -row, rows = 2, decimals = 4) |>
  cols_label(shifted = "shifted gamma", exact = "exact, FFT")
```

```text
                                   book  shifted gamma  exact, FFT
removed by a 3M aggregate limit      91             91           8
I(2M, 3M)                        1.2998         1.2999      1.3031
```

```{r}
#| label: table-6-4
book <- list(
  list(1e6, c(1e6, 2e6, 3e6, 5e6), c(29702, 30306, 30333, 30335)),
  list(2e6, c(2e6, 3e6, 5e6), c(33524, 33915, 34002)),
  list(3e6, c(3e6, 5e6), c(35421, 35781)),
  list(5e6, 5e6, 37428)
)
pieces <- list()
exact_at <- list()
for (entry in book) {
  l <- entry[[1]]
  grid <- discretize(size, h, l / h + 1, "local_moment")
  moments <- compound_moments(count, grid)
  agg <- compound_distribution(count, grid, 2^16, method = "fft")
  for (j in seq_along(entry[[2]])) {
    L <- entry[[2]][j]
    pieces[[length(pieces) + 1]] <- data.frame(
      limits = sprintf("%.0fM per claim, %.0fM aggregate", l / 1e6, L / 1e6),
      book = entry[[3]][j], shifted = moments[["mean"]] - shifted_gamma_excess(grid, L), exact = lev(agg, L))
  }
  exact_at[[as.character(l)]] <- c(at_l = lev(agg, l), unlimited = mean(agg))
}
gt(do.call(rbind, pieces), rowname_col = "limits") |>
  tab_header("Table 6.4: E[S] by per-claim and aggregate limit") |>
  fmt_number(columns = -limits, decimals = 0) |>
  cols_label(shifted = "shifted gamma", exact = "exact, FFT")
```
